obtained.how: agency copies: the human's own downloads of MDIFW's 2024 and 2016 Maine Fishing Guide PDFs (maine.gov refuses scripted fetches), indexed with getsrc.mjs --file (2024 as MDIFW_-2, 2016 as MDIFW_-2.2016); the 2021 edition was not obtained

bibliography.checked_against: the covers and contents pages of the 2016 and 2024 editions
bibliography.note: Both covers read 'Maine Fishing Guide' (MDIFW); neither prints its year. The years rest on the file names (fishingguide2016.pdf; 23-MDIFW-33-Maine-Fishing-Guide-2024-spreads.pdf) and the PDFs' creation dates (4 Feb 2016; 9 Oct 2024). The cited URL is the 2021 edition, which could not be opened (403); the rewrite could add https://www.maine.gov/ifw/docs/fishingguide2016.pdf and https://www.maine.gov/ifw/docs/23-MDIFW-33-Maine-Fishing-Guide-2024-spreads.pdf.

claims.claim: MDIFW's 713 ac for Lower is still the figure printed in the state fishing guides
claims.source_value: 2024: 'Area: 912 acres & 713 acres' (max depth 18 and 13 ft); 2016: 'Area: 912 ac & 713 ac.'
claims.location: 2024 ed., printed p. 35 (PDF p. 19, a two-page spread), Region F, Bass Fishing; 2016 ed., printed p. 27 (PDF p. 29), Region F, Bass Fishing
claims.quote: Max Depth: 18 feet, & 13 feet, Area: 912 acres & 713 acres
claims.conditions: one joint entry for 'Hot Brook Lakes (Upper & Lower)'; the guide does not say where its areas come from (they match the 1949 sheets)
claims.note: 2016 wording: 'Max Depth: 18 ft & 13 ft Area: 912 ac & 713 ac.' (PDF p. 29).

claims.claim: The fishing guides list the primary fishery as smallmouth, white perch and pickerel
claims.source_value: 'Primary Fishery: SMB, WHP, PKL' in both editions
claims.location: 2024 ed., printed p. 35 (PDF p. 19); 2016 ed., printed p. 27 (PDF p. 29)
claims.conditions: listed under 'Bass Fishing' in Region F (Penobscot Region) in both editions
claims.note: Neither guide's species key defines WHP or PKL (the 2016 key, PDF p. 7, and the 2024 key, printed p. 35 (PDF p. 19), list only trout, salmon, charr, whitefish and the two basses); reading them as white perch and chain pickerel is an obvious inference that matches the 1949 sheets' principal fisheries.

notes: Two of the three cited editions (2016, 2024) were read; the Hot Brook entry is identical in substance in both: 'Hot Brook Lakes (Upper & Lower)', Danforth, Washington County; max depth 18 and 13 ft; 912 and 713 acres; primary fishery SMB, WHP, PKL; access a town landing off Route 169 ('SR 169' in 2016, 'Rte 169' in 2024); DeLorme atlas map 45, section B-2. Both put it under Bass Fishing in Region F (Penobscot Region). The one change needed is the quotation's attribution (2024 only). The guides name only Danforth for the lakes' town; the guide gives no source for its areas, so §2.2's 'still the figure printed' is right but the guides are not an independent area measurement.
